content_preview.title: uv 0.12.23 Previews Syncing, Exporting and Inspecting uv.lock Without a Workspace Manifest
content_preview.summary: uv 0.12.23 adds a frozen-lockfile preview letting sync, export and tree run from uv.lock alone, the latest in a run of releases focused on lockfile fidelity.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Python package and project manager uv shipped version 0.12.23 on 2026-10-03, according to the [uv release page](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/tag/0.12.23). Its main addition is a preview feature, `frozen-lockfile`, that lets several `--frozen` commands operate directly on a `uv.lock` file without a workspace manifest being present.

## What Changed in 0.12.23

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise Briefing (509 words, within 300-800). Clear structure: overview, what changed, lockfile run-up, other items, explicit unknowns. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk via gunzip. source-0.html.gz (GitHub release page for 0.12.23, HTTP 200, title 'Release 0.12.23 - astral-sh/uv'): confirms 'Released on 2026-10-03', CPython 3.15.0rc3, and the four frozen-lockfile preview entries verbatim. source-1.html.gz (raw CHANGELOG.md, HTTP 200, 65,825 bytes, full file): contains every cited entry for 0.12.20, 0.12.21, 0.12.22 and 0.12.23. Verified verbatim: the four quoted preview entries (uv sync / export / tree / workspace metadata with --frozen; in the source each ends 'with `frozen-lockfile`', the article quotes the leading portion and names frozen-lockfile in its own prose), the two bug-fix quotes (alternate sources for workspace members; win_amd64 under ARM64 emulation), 0.12.20 'Reuse lockfiles when dependency declarations are semantically equivalent' and lockfile-normalization preview, 0.12.21 'Omit empty `[manifest]` tables...' and resolution-inputs preview, 0.12.22 recorded default groups / dependency-group Python requirements for workspace members and non-project roots, 'Use each selected workspace member's recorded default groups during frozen sync', UV_PYTHON_ARCH ('select an interpreter architecture independently of its Python version'), and CPython 3.10.22, 3.11.17, 3.12.15, 3.13.16, 3.14.8. Both manifest suspicious_patterns entries are null; nothing to override. Both body URLs are in article.sources and vice versa. Nothing rests on docs.astral.sh (not cited anywhere).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: (1) Feature name 'frozen-lockfile' and the four commands (uv sync, uv export, uv tree, uv workspace metadata, each with --frozen) match the changelog and release page exactly; 'without a workspace manifest' is used as in the source and the article states the source does not explain use cases. (2) The 0.12.22 release date appears nowhere in the article (changelog says 2026-10-01, release page reportedly differs); only 0.12.23's 2026-10-03 date is given, and it is confirmed by both snapshots. (3) The link between the 0.12.22 lockfile-recording changes and the new feature is explicitly labelled as an inference ('that link is an inference from the sequence of entries rather than a statement by the project') and repeated as an unknown under 'What We Don't Know'; it is not stated as project fact. (4) 'frozen-lockfile' is described as a preview feature and 'experimental', never as stable; the changelog lists it under 'Preview features'. The 'experimental' gloss is a mild paraphrase of preview status but is not misleading. (5) The changelog snapshot is complete and contains all cited entries.
